faq.a: Light travels in straight lines and cannot bend around a solid object. When something blocks the light, the area behind it gets no light, and that dark shape is a shadow.

faq.q: Why is my shadow long in the morning?
faq.a: In the morning the Sun is low, so its rays arrive at a shallow slant. Your body blocks those slanting rays over a long stretch of ground, making a long shadow.
Your shadow is shortest around midday, when the Sun is highest in the sky. Then the light comes from nearly overhead and your body blocks only a small patch of ground.
asks: Why is my shadow small at noon?
What time is the shortest shadow?

faq.q: Which way does my shadow point?
faq.a: A shadow always points away from the Sun. In the morning it points roughly west, in the evening roughly east, and at noon in Britain it points north.
asks: Why does my shadow move during the day?
Does a shadow point the same way all day?

faq.q: How does a sundial tell the time?
faq.a: A sundial has a pointer called a gnomon. As the Sun moves across the sky, the gnomon's shadow swings round the dial, and its position shows the time.
asks: How did people tell time with shadows?

facts: A shadow forms because light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through an opaque object.
In the Northern Hemisphere outside the tropics, a noon shadow points roughly north.
Winter shadows are longer than summer ones because the midday Sun is lower in winter.

quiz.say: At what time of day is your shadow shortest?
quiz.why: Around midday the Sun is highest, so light comes from nearly overhead and the shadow is shortest.

wrong.0: The morning Sun is low, so shadows are long.
wrong.2: The Sun is low before sunset, so shadows are long again.

quiz.say: It is early morning and the Sun has just risen in the east. Which way does your shadow point?
quiz.why: A shadow points away from the Sun, so with the Sun in the east it points west.

wrong.1: That would point towards the Sun, but shadows fall away from it.
wrong.2: A shadow is under you only when the Sun is directly overhead.
